item.title: Re: Why is this Euclid?
item.content:encoded: You're spot-on. It really is almost straddling the line between safe and euclid, but there's enough potential for havoc, and enough unanswered questions that makes it solidly euclid. At least in my opinion.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Honestly, that's what I was going for when I wrote it. I remember reading some of the metacommentary about the more ridiculous entries (not naming any names) and I decided that my small contribution would avoid that as best I could. Basically I really wanted to capture the essence of what I loved about the SCP Foundation.

I can't believe that was almost 10 years ago now.

item.title: Re: Why is this Euclid?
item.content:encoded: Because only part of it is completely contained. The baby keeps phasing in and out of existence and has shown to be dangerous under certain conditions. It may just act in cases like the last one, but that's a huge may. Observation is required, perhaps not super-active one, but it's not like they can merely lock it in and call it a day.

item.title: Containment issue
item.content:encoded:
Why is this thing housed in plexiglass? even thick plexiglass?

It COMPELS people who see it to lay their hands upon the bar, triggering it's effect. It should be housed in an OPAQUE container. Basically, any crate/steel box big enough to hold it.

Other than that, the concept is acceptable.

so, if the pusher/victim of the SCP dies within 2 hours, the "baby" vanishes, and the carriage degrades within 30 minutes?
if they last for 2 hours, the baby attacks, eating them, and … presumably goes on a rampage.

I REALLY wonder about the origins of this one. :D

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Although the 'haunted' feel to this article seems to me like something we'd ordinarily steer clear of as far as SCP ideas, I do really like this article. One thing I did notice in particular was that the [DATA EXPUNGED] sections weren't like running into the reading equivalent of a brick wall, but instead only left out part of an idea while detailing the result a little bit and then maybe leaving out a bit more, and so on. Like so: SCP-382 does [something horrible], feasting on the D's now-mummified corpse, and proceeding to [do something even more horrible]. There's the initial "ok there's some shit goin on now" followed by "ohsweetjesusWHAT" and "for fuck's sake what's it doing now". Which was delightful. I may reference, quote and/or cite this article in future comments regarding issues with [DATA EXPUNGED].

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'm with comwilson on the numbering.

If you have a main object and a secondary product or manifestation I can see the main one being SCP-XXX and the extras XXX-1 to whatever. But certain things don't have a main component so much as they have distinct and dependent parts, like this one. So I think it's valid to have 382-1 and 382-2 rather than an original 382. 382 just represents everything under containment in this case.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
If you're referring to "The subject will continue to interact with SCP-382 up until just under two hours…" I just meant that the subject interacts with SCP-382-1 and SCP-382-2 at the same time.

Edit: Also, "…subject has died and SCP-382 has reset." means that they both returned to the state they were in before interacting with the subject.
